themes.title: Hot CPI pushes Bitcoin to an 11-week low
themes.summary: October consumer prices rose 0.4% versus 0.3% expected; Bitcoin fell to as low as about $72,787 after the release, its weakest level since Aug. 21, as bets on a December Fed hike firmed.

themes.title: ETF outflows continue
themes.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen roughly $1.5 billion of outflows since Nov. 2, and BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF has had about $1.66 billion of outflows over seven trading sessions.

themes.title: Miner selling adds supply
themes.summary: MARA Holdings sold 13,597 BTC, about $1.1 billion, over six weeks and has said it plans to sell more.

themes.title: BitMine keeps adding Ether
themes.summary: BitMine Immersion bought 9,587 ETH last week, bringing its holdings to about 6.07 million ETH, roughly 4.97% of circulating supply, though Ether still fell on the day.

themes.title: NYSE picks Avalanche for tokenized trading
themes.summary: The NYSE chose Avalanche to settle trades on a planned 24/7 tokenized securities platform; the plan is still pending.

categories.name: Majors (BTC/ETH)
categories.note: Both fell after the CPI report, with Ether (down about 3.3%) weaker than Bitcoin (down about 1.5%) over 24 hours.

categories.name: Privacy coins
categories.note: Zcash was among the biggest 24-hour decliners, down about 11.5% (CoinMarketCap).

categories.name: Layer 2 / AI tokens
categories.note: Arbitrum fell about 10.6% and Venice Token about 10.8% over 24 hours, among the weakest large tokens (CoinMarketCap).

categories.name: Tokenized assets / RWA
categories.note: The NYSE's plan to use Avalanche for tokenized securities settlement kept attention on real-world-asset projects, though the platform is still pending.

watch_list.why: The hotter CPI report raised expectations for a December rate hike, and rate expectations have weighed on crypto.
Tuesday's low near $72,787 was the weakest level since late August and close to Sunday's low.
Continued redemptions from spot ETFs and further selling by miners such as MARA would add supply to the market.

movers.name: Gram (GRAM, formerly Toncoin)
movers.note: Top 24-hour gainer on CoinMarketCap's gainers list.

movers.name: Pieverse (PIEVERSE)
movers.note: Gave back part of Monday's surge; the largest 24-hour decliner on CoinMarketCap's list.
